offered_action_specs.name: rollback_deploy
offered_action_specs.description: Roll one service back to the settings it ran before its latest deploy, as the deploy log records them. Code plans it from that log, not from your tools' results, so you can name it even when they cannot see deploys: if the log holds no deploy of that service to undo, or the service changed since, code refuses it. Its container is recreated, so the service pauses while it restarts. Money already booked wrong stays wrong: a rollback stops new damage, and repairs nothing.

proposed.why: No tool calls are left, and the results show how evt_000272 came to be booked twice.

findings.cause: ledger-consumer booked one provider event twice. evt_000272 (payment.succeeded, pay_000247, $104.44) reached us twice, 0.5 s apart. webhook-receiver queued both copies to provider-events partition 1, at offsets 123 and 124. The provider resending a webhook is expected: delivery is at-least-once. The ledger-consumer has to dedup these, and it did not. At offset 123 it ran its dedup insert (INSERT INTO processed_events ... ON CONFLICT (event_id) DO NOTHING) and then posted. At offset 124 it did no processed_events insert or check at all and went straight to INSERT transactions and entries. It logged 'posted' both times, creating ledger transactions 272 and 275. That double entry puts the ledger $104.44 ahead of the provider, which fails posted_exactly_once and matches_provider. payment-confirmer handled both copies idempotently (already_confirmed), so our payment record is correct and only the ledger is wrong.

evidence.shows: Re-running the money check after waiting to settle reproduces the failure. evt_000272 (pay_000247, $104.44) was posted twice, as transactions 272 and 275. The ledger is +$104.44 against the provider, all of it on pay_000247. Payments and refunds agree with the provider, so this is not a timing gap.
ledger-consumer logged 'posted' for evt_000272 twice: from provider-events/1＠123 at 22:17:49.923 and from ＠124 at 22:17:50.668, with different trace ids.
webhook-receiver queued evt_000272 twice, at offsets 123 and 124, so two Kafka messages exist for one event.

First delivery: the receiver answered 200 in 3 ms. The ledger span runs INSERT processed_events ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, then inserts the transaction and its entries. The confirmer reports already_confirmed.

Second delivery: the receiver answered 200 again. The ledger span starts about 248 ms in and inserts the transaction and entries with no processed_events insert or check at all, outcome posted. The confirmer reports already_confirmed.
The ledger does sometimes count duplicates as already_processed (21 in the last 10 min), so dedup works on some path. It was skipped for offset 124.
ledger-consumer logged no warnings or errors in the last hour. There is no sign of a restart, a rebalance or a dedup-store failure explaining the skip.

findings.left_open: I don't know why the dedup step was skipped for offset 124 but works for other events. It could be a changed or faulty LEDGER_HANDLER, or a code path that bypasses processed_events. The handler might also not check the ON CONFLICT result. recent_deploys failed (c4: Docker did not answer), so I could not see the ledger-consumer's settings or whether it was recently redeployed. I don't know whether other events were also double-posted and are still unchecked; the money check found only this one. I don't know why the provider resent a webhook that had been acknowledged with 200 in 3 ms. That is expected at-least-once behavior, but its trigger is unknown. Service health and restarts were not checked.
